Senses.Explanation: A closing question that turns a finished statement back on the assembly, demanding to know whether what was just given has been fully taken in. Song-era hall records set the hinge: Yuanwu Keqin closes a ruling that proceeding either way still serves the true eye with the question and a verse that leaves crown-striding arrivals wordless; Dahui Zonggao follows his nothing-was-ever-born ruling with the question, a leap-beyond-the-void verse, and descent from the seat, and in a general discourse asks it once the six senses are sealed, before striking the seat with his whisk; Hongzhi Zhengjue sets it after inherited lines on light within dark and dark within light. Later hall records keep the same closing hinge: Meixi Fudu strikes the incense table with the whisk and only then asks, ruling that what is fully taken in may be called Buddha-nature or not; Baichi Xingyuan ends an inaugural hall address on it; Yuan'an Liao caps a no-master-here, no-acolyte pronouncement with it; Poshan Haiming lifts the staff, strikes once, and asks over a never-born, never-destroyed pronouncement; Shenfeng Xian asks it of the assembly on an ordination day before turning to the ceremony's business; Miyun Yuanwu follows the question with a shout and leaves the seat.
